label: MARRIAGE REPAIR

cover.headline: How to apologize *so it lands*
cover.sub: 5 parts of an apology that helps repair.

points.heading: Name exactly what you did
points.body: “Sorry for everything” is too big to take in. Be specific about the one thing.
points.panel: “I’m sorry I snapped at you in front of the kids.”

points.heading: Leave out the “but”
points.body: Whatever comes after “but” erases what came before it. Your reasons can wait for another talk.

points.heading: Say how it affected him
points.body: It shows you’ve thought about his side, not only your own guilt.
points.panel: “That must have been embarrassing, and you didn’t deserve it.”

points.heading: Say what you’ll do differently
points.body: Keep it small and real. A promise you can keep is worth more than a grand one.
points.panel: “Next time I’ll step away before I raise my voice.”

points.heading: Give him time
points.body: An apology is an offer, and he gets to take it at his own pace.
points.panel: “You don’t have to say anything right now.”

close.save: Save this for when you need it.

caption:
A good apology is one of the most useful skills in a marriage, and few of us were ever taught how to make one.

This isn’t about taking all the blame or apologizing for things that weren’t yours. It’s about owning your part clearly, so repair can start. Here are the five parts.
